harry_cs: Tideway Labs POC: their serverless warmup triggers a few 401s then a sustained 429 spike. Happening ~20-40s after cold start. Can eng advise?
lee_eng: thanks. 401->429 during warmup usually means ephemeral token rotation overlaps + aggressive fanout. Can you paste the warmup request?
harry_cs: snippet from their sidecar: 
```
POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral_jwt>
Content-Type: application/json
{"model":"rwdllm-3b","input":"warmup"}
```
harry_cs: they mint ephemeral_jwt every 30s and run 10 parallel warmup threads on cold start. Logs show 2x 401 then many 429s.
oncall-bot: alert: tideway-poc (client:twd-900) 5m 429 rate rose 1% -> 38% at 3375000068. Top route: /v1/chat.
rachel_se: hypothesis: token provider returning empty/short token in some refresh races -> 401, concurrent retries push them over soft concurrency -> 429. Mobile/function warmup fanout amplifies it.
lee_eng: quick customer fixes to try now: 1) cache tokens per-worker for >=70s to prevent refresh overlap; 2) add jitter + exponential backoff on 401s; 3) cap warmup parallelism (try 3). Example JS patch: 
```
const c = new RedwoodClient({
  tokenProvider: cachedProvider(75),
  maxConcurrency: 3,
  authRetry: {attempts:4, baseDelayMs:200, jitter:true}
});
```
rachel_se: if they can't deploy quickly we can request a temporary soft-cap bump (+2 slots) and a 45s token-grace window for twd-900. Ops approval needed.
harry_cs: customer prefers self-serve. I'll send the SDK snippet and ask them to run 50 staged warmups sequentially then report 429 rate after 20m. If >25% we escalate.
abe_ae: flagging renewal risk if POC delays >48h. Keep me posted.
lee_eng: action owners: Harry -> share snippet + runbook; Rachel -> ops escalation template; I-> prepare brief on token-grace pros/cons.
